units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "This encouraged a brief recovery before Black Tuesday."
units.note: "for a day" is not in any pinned source, which says only "a brief recovery". After Black Thursday the market held through Friday 25 October (Dow up about half a percent, fool.com 2013-10-25) and a Saturday half-session (298.97 close, implied by the source: 260.64 + 38.33), and the slide resumed on Monday 28 October. That is two sessions, not one day.
units.fix: The crash that paused
units.resolved: Applied the checker's fix: The crash that paused

units.evidence: [Commons Crowd_outside_nyse.jpg] "A solemn crowd gathers outside the Stock Exchange after the crash. 1929."
units.note: Matches the file description. Commons dates the photo "Taken on 29 October 1929" (Black Tuesday), which fits "after the crash". Frames 2 to 4 narrate Black Thursday over the same photo but do not claim it shows that day.

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "On October 24, \"Black Thursday\", the market lost 11% of its value at the opening bell."
units.note: Stands on the pinned sentence. Secondary accounts vary between "opened 11% lower" and "fell 11% in the first hours", but the caption matches the pinned source. 24 October 1929 was a Thursday.

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "They chose Richard Whitney, vice president of the Exchange, to act on their behalf." / "With the bankers' financial resources behind him, Whitney placed a bid to purchase 25,000 shares of U.S. Steel at $205 per share, a price well above the current market."
units.note: Supported. "had Whitney bid" fairly compresses "chose Whitney to act on their behalf" plus "with the bankers' financial resources behind him".

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "succeeded in halting the slide. The Dow Jones Industrial Average recovered, closing down only 6.38 points (2.09%) for the day."
units.note: 2.09% rounds to "about 2 percent". Supported.

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "for a total drop of 68.90 points, or 23.05% in two days" + [Commons NYT file] "on the day after \"Black Tuesday\""
units.note: Supported. The 23.05% runs from Saturday 26 October's close (298.97) to Tuesday's (230.07); 68.90/298.97 = 23.05%. Monday 28 October was the next Monday after Black Thursday. Note that the image is only part of the front page plus a table from page 31 (see media.m5).

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "peaking at 381.17 on September 3, 1929" / "July 8, 1932, when it closed at 41.22 ... concluding an 89.2% loss" / "did not return to its peak close of September 3, 1929, for 25 years, until November 23, 1954"
units.note: The arithmetic holds: (381.17 - 41.22) / 381.17 = 89.19%, measured from the September 1929 peak, so "89 percent below its 1929 peak" is right.

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "closing down only 6.38 points (2.09%) for the day."
units.note: Key right (2.09%). "About 11 percent" was the early fall, not the close. "About 25 percent" was never the close on Black Thursday (the two-day fall of 28 and 29 October was 23%). Both wrong choices are clearly wrong.

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Wall Street crash of 1929] "This encouraged a brief recovery before Black Tuesday."
units.note: The second sentence is supported (89.19% from 381.17 to 41.22). "for a day" is not in the pinned source: the market held through Friday 25 and the Saturday 26 October half-session, and the slide resumed on Monday 28 October.
units.fix: Bankers briefly stopped Black Thursday's slide. By July 1932 the Dow stood 89 percent below its 1929 peak.
units.resolved: Applied the checker's fix: Bankers briefly stopped Black Thursday's slide. By July 1932 the Dow stood 89 percent below its 1929 peak.

units.evidence: "It was previously considered extinct."

"Prior to the 1902 eruption, there were no historical records of activity on the volcano. It was previously considered extinct." / [Commons] "Der Vulkan Santa María in Guatemala während des Ausbruchs im Jahr 1902."

Pinned timeline: "By 20:00, the volcano produced a large eruption column" (24 Oct); "Large lithics ... at 01:00 of 25 October, signifying that the eruption had entered its Plinian stage"; "By 11:00, the eruption had reached its climax." The sextant sentence gives no time.
units.note: The caption ties the 27 to 29 km sextant estimate to the column of "the evening of 24 October" ("estimated its height"). The pinned source gives no time for the estimate, and by its own timeline the Plinian stage began at 01:00 and peaked at 11:00 on 25 October. Oregon State's volcano site puts the ~28 km column at the largest Plinian phase on 25 October. The two facts are fused into one moment.
units.fix: On the evening of 24 October, an ash column rose amid lightning. A ship's captain later put its height by sextant at 27 to 29 kilometres.
units.resolved: Applied the checker's fix: On the evening of 24 October, an ash column rose amid lightning. A ship's captain later put its height by sextant at 27 to 29 kilometres.

units.note: Supported. The source equates the main eruption (lead, "no more than 20 hours") with the 18-to-20-hour Plinian phase. units.note: Supported. His Mendel paper appeared in Berichte der Deutschen Botanischen Gesellschaft vol. 18 (1900), registered 24 April 1900, so "publishing in 1900" holds whichever 1900 paper is meant.

units.note: Supported. It also matches the standard account of Correns's Mirabilis albomaculata crosses.

"while Mendelian traits behave independently of the sex of the source parent" / "since the chloroplasts come exclusively from the mother in most angiosperms"
units.note: Supported. "here" applies the "most angiosperms" rule to Mirabilis, which is correct. The caption wisely skips the source's garbled iojap paragraph (iojap is a maize gene, not Correns's Mirabilis mechanism).

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Heritability] "For example, it is incorrect to say that since the heritability of personality traits is about 0.6 ..." vs Vukasović & Bratko 2015, Psychological Bulletin (PubMed 25961374): pooled heritability of personality 0.40 (twin studies 0.47)
units.note: The pinned source gives 0.6 only as the premise of an example of a wrong inference. The caption states it as fact. The largest meta-analysis puts personality heritability at about 0.40 (0.47 in twin studies), so "about 0.6" is the top of the range, not the typical estimate.
units.fix: Heritability is a statistic about such variation. For personality it has been put as high as 0.6, which is easy to misread as 60 percent of you.
